title: Geometric connectedness is tested by finite separable extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $Y$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Then $Y$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if for every field extension $k'/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] that is finite ($\dim_kk'<\infty$) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] the base change $Y_{k'}=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

proof.text: The forward implication specializes geometric connectedness to the pullback along any finite separable field extension.

For the converse, set L = SeparableClosure k. The degree-one test gives a point of Y by projecting a point of Y_k. Since Spec k is a one-point space, the base change Y_L is nonempty. To prove it connected it suffices that every clopen subset is empty or the whole space.

Suppose Y_L has a nontrivial clopen subset U. Apply the finite invariant partition lemma to obtain a finite intermediate field K and a nontrivial Aut(L/K)-invariant clopen subset V on the iterated base change (Y_K)_L. The extension K/k is separable because it is intermediate in the separable closure, so the assumed test makes Y_K connected.

Descend V and its complement as closed subsets A and B of Y_K using Galois closed-subset descent. The base-change projection is surjective. Injectivity of inverse images then shows B = Aᶜ. Thus A is clopen in connected Y_K, so A is empty or the whole space. Pulling back contradicts nonemptiness of both V and Vᶜ. Complement invariance follows from bijectivity of the base-change automorphisms; their isomorphism property follows from the pullback square of Spec of a ring equivalence. This is the proved private helper invariant_clopen_eq_empty_or_univ.

Having proved Y_L connected, apply geometric connectedness over a separably closed field to its structure map, then the field-extension checking equivalence to descend geometric connectedness from L to k.
